decisions.statement: A run's answer has the code the run exited with.
A run's answer carries how many errors were counted.
A run's answer carries every finding named.
A run's answer carries where the run could not look and why.
A run's answer has nothing more.
A run whose answer cannot be read says why rather than an empty list.
The findings are read from the first line printed that parses as an object with diagnostics.
A root holding no linter is a run that was never made rather than a tree that came back clean.
The paths named are looked at in batches one command line holds.
The batches are read back as one answer.
A batch that could not be looked at answers for the whole run.
A run is held to two processors rather than to every processor the machine has.
A run takes longer for being held there.
Every run of the linter is held there, a run made to format among them.
The linter is told how many processors to take by the environment it is given.
Biome says of its own JSON reporter that the reporter is unstable and may change between patches.
This module reads the JSON reporter anyway.
That reporter is the only shape of Biome's answer a machine can take.
Nothing here says which rules run.
The checks made are the checks the linter's configuration sets.
A run has no configuration of its own.
How findings are reported is not answered here.
The printed output belongs to the caller that asked for the run.
How much of the printed output a caller may have belongs to the caller that asked for the run.
What exit follows belongs to the caller that asked for the run.

definition: running the linter over what is there and reading back what it found, changing nothing
